metaTitle: Best 36 Inch Griddles for Big Cooks, 2026
metaDescription: Six 36 inch outdoor gas griddles compared by measured square inches, plate steel, burner zones and fuel type to help you feed a crowd well.
expertTake: The Weber Slate 36 inch is the best pick here for its rust-resistant carbon steel plate and a cabinet that keeps gear dry, but it runs on natural gas so it suits a fixed outdoor kitchen. The Feasto 36 inch is the value pick with a thick plate and 720 square inches. Skip this size if you cook for fewer than six people, because a 36 inch plate heats a lot of steel you will not use. Whichever you choose, budget for a cover and a spare fuel supply.
introParagraphs: A 36 inch griddle is the size where a cart stops being a gadget and becomes a piece of outdoor kitchen furniture. It cooks for a crowd, runs several burners and demands a place on the patio plus a spare cylinder or a gas line. Cooks who move up from a smaller unit often find the extra width changes how they plan a meal, not just how much they make.

At this width the questions change. You stop asking whether it will fit your hobby and start asking how evenly the far corners heat, how many real zones you get and whether the fuel source suits where you live.

products.name: Weber Slate 36 Inch Rust-Resistant Griddle, Natural Gas
products.description:
The Slate 36 is built like a piece of outdoor furniture. The carbon steel plate arrives pre-seasoned and is marketed as rust resistant, with edge to edge heat across four burners. A closed cabinet below keeps oil, tools and a spare cylinder dry, and a flip-up side table gives you prep room.

The natural gas configuration is the one to understand before buying. It runs from a house gas line, which is ideal for a built-in outdoor kitchen and useless for a campsite. If you want propane, check which version you are actually ordering, because the listing here specifies natural gas.

Weber's plate is among the thickest consumer plates, and thick steel is why it spreads heat evenly without hot spots near the burners. That mass also takes longer to come up to temperature and longer to cool, so expect to light it a few minutes earlier than a thin plate. Ownership is lighter than on bare steel, but not zero. Pre-seasoned does not mean maintenance free, so scrape, wipe and oil after each cook and cover it in wet weather. For a permanent backyard setup it is the most polished choice in this lineup.
products.bestFor: Owners with a gas line who want a rust-aware, cabinet-equipped centrepiece.
pros: Pre-seasoned carbon steel plate ready out of the box
Four burners with even edge to edge heat
Flip-up side table adds prep room
cons: Natural gas version needs a house gas line
Thick plate is slow to heat and slow to cool
Fixed cabinet cart is not portable

products.name: Blackstone 2439 36 Inch Griddle with Air Fryer Combo, 768 sq in
products.description:
The 2439 adds an integrated air fryer and a hood to the standard Blackstone four zone layout. The listing credits it with 768 square inches of cooking space, a little above the typical 720 for this class, and the Omnivore plate carries the faster preheat and wind guards the brand is known for.

The air fryer is a genuine second cooking zone, which changes the workflow: fries or wings can finish beside burgers on the plate. It also adds one more thing to clean and one more place for grease to collect.

Against the plain 2322, the 2439 swaps simplicity for versatility. If you will use the air fryer weekly, it pays for itself in convenience. If you will not, it is a premium for a feature that sits idle and the 2322 is the cleaner buy. Plan on the same plate routine as any Blackstone: scrape hot, oil thinly, cover outdoors.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want fried sides and griddle mains from one machine.
pros: Integrated air fryer widens the menu
cons: Air fryer is extra to clean and maintain
More expensive than the plain 36 inch model

products.name: Blackstone 2322 36 Inch Omnivore Griddle with Hood
products.description:
The 2322 is the plain version of Blackstone's 36 inch design: four independently controlled burners, an Omnivore plate with wind guards and a hood. It is the benchmark that the others are measured against.

Propane makes it flexible, since you can use it in a yard without a gas line or take it to an event if you have a truck. The hood keeps the plate cleaner than an open model and allows steaming and melting.

Compared with the Weber Slate, it gives up the cabinet and the thicker plate but also the natural gas lock-in. Compared with the 2439, it skips the air fryer and the extra cleaning. That makes it the dependable middle option in this size. Maintenance is the standard flat top routine, and a soft cover is smart through wet months.
products.bestFor: Hosts who want a proven four zone propane griddle with a hood.
pros: Four independent zones on a 36 inch plate

products.name: Cuisinart CGG-0036 36 Inch Four Burner Gas Griddle, 760 sq in
products.description:
Cuisinart's 36 inch griddle lists 760 square inches of cold-rolled steel, which is the plate material that research points to for even heat and holding a seasoning layer. Four burners sit beneath it.

The standout is the dual grease management system, with two front cups that make it easier to drain fat from either end of the plate. On a wide griddle, a single drain can leave the far side swimming in oil, so two collection points are a real convenience.

The plate is bare steel, so the usual seasoning and rust discipline applies. The listing does not mention a hood, so treat a soft cover as a necessity rather than an add-on. Against the Blackstones it is a more conventional design with fewer extras, which suits a buyer who wants the basics done well.
products.bestFor: Buyers who prioritise grease control and a straightforward steel plate.
pros: Two front grease cups for easier draining
cons: No hood mentioned in the listing
Bare steel requires oiling and covering

products.name: Char-Broil 36 Inch Performance Series Deluxe Griddle with Cart
products.description:
Char-Broil's Deluxe model is built around a dedicated sear zone that the listing says reaches temperatures over 700 degrees Fahrenheit, plus a separation system that gives you two cooking zones with different heat. It is the griddle for cooks who want one hot end for searing and one gentler end for finishing.

Two big zones are less flexible than four independent burners, but the sear claim speaks to a real gap: many griddles run warm rather than hot. A dedicated hot end lets you crust a steak or brown a smash burger.

The Deluxe adds features over the plain Char-Broil 36 listed beside it, including the deluxe cart. The trade is a more complex build and a higher tier on the price scale. Ownership follows the standard plate routine, with the added tip that a very hot zone burns off oil faster, so keep it seasoned.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a true hot sear end and a cooler finishing end.
pros: Dedicated sear zone over 700 F per the listing
cons: Two main zones are less flexible than four
Hot zone needs careful seasoning upkeep

products.name: Feasto 36 Inch 4-Burner Griddle, 63,000 BTU, 720 sq in
products.description:
Feasto is the lowest cost route to a genuine 36 inch plate. The listing quotes 720 square inches, matching the rule of thumb for this class, and a thick hot-rolled steel top that it says resists warping.

Burner output is generous, with the listing counting 63,000 BTU in total including a side burner. That headline figure matters less than the plate, but it does mean the machine can recover fast after a cold load.

The tradeoff is brand maturity. Parts supply and long-term support are less certain than with Weber, Blackstone or Cuisinart, so check that replacement knobs and igniters are available before you buy. It makes sense for a household that wants the space and will accept a lesser known name.
products.bestFor: Value shoppers who want a full 36 inch plate and a side burner.
pros: 720 square inches on a 36 inch plate
Hot-rolled steel top resists warping per the listing
Side burner adds a stockpot station
Large output reserves for cold loads
cons: Brand support and parts supply are less proven

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 36 inch class plate is around 720 square inches, and the labels hide wide variation. The Cuisinart lists 760, the Blackstone 2439 768 and the Feasto 720. A few dozen square inches is one extra row of burgers, so compare the figure, not the width. The mistake we see most is judging the plate by the label on the box and then finding that the usable area is smaller once the lip and grease channel are taken out.

Cold-rolled steel in the 4 mm to 6 mm range spreads heat edge to edge, and the Weber Slate's plate is quoted at the heavy end of consumer plates. Thinner plates warp when frozen patties hit hot steel. On a 36 inch plate a warp is easy to see and hard to cure. On a wide plate any warp shows as pooled oil on one side, so it is worth reading owner comments for that exact complaint before you commit.

Propane works anywhere, while natural gas only works at a fixed line. The Slate in this guide is natural gas, the rest are propane. Decide before you shop, because converting later is not always possible. Switching fuel later is rarely a simple swap, so settle the question first and shop only within that group.

Four independent burners let you sear, cook and hold at once. The Blackstones and Weber list four, Char-Broil offers two broad zones plus a hot sear area. Zones matter more than total BTU. Ask yourself how many dishes you actually cook at different temperatures, because many cooks never use more than two zones.

A wide plate needs good drainage. The Cuisinart's two front cups and the Feasto's grease cup show different approaches. Look at where grease goes and how far you reach to empty it. A grease cup you cannot reach without lifting the hood or crouching becomes a chore you start to skip.

At this size a hood or closed cabinet makes a difference. The Weber has a cabinet, the 2322 and 2439 have hoods, and the Cuisinart lacks one in its listing. A soft cover helps everywhere. Cabinets also hide clutter and keep a spare cylinder out of the rain, which is useful when the griddle is the centre of the patio.

specDecoder.meaning: The usable plate area. It is smaller than width times depth because of the edge lip and the grease channel.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Blackstone 2439 lists 768, the Cuisinart 760 and the Feasto 720.

specDecoder.meaning: The sum of all burner ratings including any side burner. It indicates fuel use, not cooking quality.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Feasto lists 63,000 BTU including a side burner.

specDecoder.meaning: Cold-rolled, hot-rolled or carbon steel. It determines heat spread and how the plate wears.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Cuisinart is cold-rolled, the Feasto hot-rolled, the Weber carbon steel.

specDecoder.meaning: Independently controlled burners. They allow different temperatures at the same time.
specDecoder.watchFor: Char-Broil's TRU-Zonal gives two zones, not four.

specDecoder.meaning: Propane or natural gas. It sets where the griddle can live.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Weber is natural gas in this listing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Plate area and steel
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared listed square inches and plate material, since both decide how much food cooks evenly. The Blackstone 2439 at 768 and the Cuisinart at 760 led on area. The Weber's thick carbon steel stood out on material. Ratings of ownership cost leaned on seasoning effort and parts availability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Zone control
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted separate burner controls and checked for a sear zone. Four independent burners score best for flexibility, while Char-Broil's sear zone earns credit for a specific job. Zones outranked BTU in our ordering. Where a listing was silent on a feature we did not assume it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weather and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for hoods, cabinets and rust resistance. The Weber's cabinet and the Blackstones' hoods earned points. Open plates lost marks outdoors. Placement limits were treated as a cost, not a flaw.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fuel and placement
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted natural gas versus propane and what that means for placement. The Weber suits a fixed kitchen, the propane units suit most yards. Flexibility counted. Where two models shared a design we compared their extras.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We scanned listings for recurring themes such as warping plates, uneven heat and shaky frames. These shaped the cons and the ranking, not any numeric score. Cons reflect repeat themes only.

rows: Cabinet and carbon steel, or air fryer combo

cards.label: Propane
cards.text: The Blackstones, Cuisinart, Char-Broil and Feasto run on propane. You can place them anywhere in the yard and swap a cylinder in a minute.

cards.label: Natural gas
cards.text: The Weber Slate here uses a house line. It never runs out mid-cook, but it fixes the cart to a connection.

howToChoose.note: Choose natural gas only if you have a line and a permanent spot. Everyone else should choose propane.

howToChoose.subheading: For Cooking for 10 or More Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A plate near 720 square inches or more, four independent zones and enough fuel capacity for a long session. Keep a spare cylinder or a gas line.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Blackstone 2439 at 768 square inches, the Cuisinart at 760 and the Feasto at 720 all clear the bar. The Weber Slate adds the cabinet for tools.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You are building an outdoor kitchen and want the Weber Slate's cabinet and thick plate, or the 2439's air fryer.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You will use the griddle a few times a month. The Feasto or Cuisinart gives you the plate size without the extras.

maintenance.why: Hot residue lifts easily and cold residue carbonizes. A wide plate multiplies the cleanup if you wait.
A thin film keeps moisture off the steel. At 36 inches there is more surface to rust.
Wide plates collect a lot of fat. A full cup overflows onto the cart.
Several thin oil layers heated to smoke restore the non-stick surface. It also seals pits.
Apply soapy water and look for bubbles. Replace leaking parts before use.

faq.q: Is a 36 inch griddle too big for a home?
faq.a: It is the right size for six or more regular eaters and a space of about two metres of patio. For smaller households a 28 inch plate cooks the same way with less steel to heat.

faq.q: How many people does 720 square inches feed?
faq.a: Roughly a dozen burgers in a pass, so it comfortably feeds eight to ten. The research rule of thumb is that a 36 inch class plate is around 720 square inches.

faq.q: Propane or natural gas for a 36 inch?
faq.a: Propane for flexibility, natural gas for a permanent kitchen. The Weber Slate in this guide is natural gas and needs a house gas line.
It helps outdoors by protecting the plate and enabling steaming. Without one, buy a soft cover and oil after every cook.

faq.q: Is more BTU better on a 36 inch plate?
faq.a: Not by itself. Thickness and zone control matter more than a big total, and a very high BTU number on a thin plate causes hot spots.

faq.q: Can it go on a balcony?
faq.a: Rules depend on fire code, your lease or HOA and the manufacturer. A 36 inch propane cart is a poor balcony candidate in almost every case.
